newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Domenici says budget talks define issues.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Domenici says budget talks define issues.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici said Wednesday congressional and White House staff will meet over the next three weeks in an attempt to narrow differences on four to five key budget issues.
The New Mexico Republican said he was pleased with the nearly two hour meeting at the White House with President Clinton and other congressional budget leaders.

"It was not intended to bridge any gaps. It was intended to define the issues. We did that," he told reporters off the Senate floor. "The president stayed there for an hour and forty minutes or more. There was a frank and clear discussion of our differences and we pulled no punches. Everybody understands the differences are big."
Asked which issues were on the list, Domenici said it would be the major ones such as Medicare.

Some key differences between the White House and the Republican-led Congress include a downward adjustment in the consumer price index recommended by many in Congress and the gap between White House and congressional estimates on economic growth.
Congress will be on recess for the next two weeks.
